string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China and one of the world's oldest cities. With over three millennia of history, it served as the seat of power for the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. Today it is China's political, cultural, and educational center, home to iconic landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, Tiananmen Square, and the Temple of Heaven. Beijing hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and is a global city with a population of over twenty million.

Shanghai is China's largest city and a global financial hub. Located on the Yangtze River Delta, it has been a major trading port since the 19th century. The city blends modern skyscrapers like the Oriental Pearl Tower and Shanghai Tower with the historic Bund waterfront. Shanghai is the world's busiest container port and a center for finance, technology, and culture, attracting visitors with its museums, shopping districts, and vibrant food scene.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in southwest China and the largest and most populous city proper in the world. Situated at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, it is known for its hilly terrain, misty weather, and hot pot cuisine. Chongqing serves as an economic center in the upstream Yangtze region and is a major manufacturing and transportation hub, with the famous Three Gorges located nearby on the Yangtze River.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality in northern China, located on the coast of the Bohai Sea. It borders Beijing to the northwest and has a history as a treaty port with foreign concessions, reflected in its colonial-era architecture. Today Tianjin is a major port city and industrial base, known for its Tianjin Eye Ferris wheel, ancient culture street, and the waterfront Hai River. It forms part of the Jing-Jin-Ji megalopolis surrounding Beijing.
